question: In which of the following are the songs of Alvar saints compiled?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Divya Prabandham**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Divya Prabandham** is a revered collection of hymns composed by the Alvar saints, who were devotional poets in South India.

• The term "Divya Prabandham" translates to "Sacred Compilation" in Tamil, emphasizing its spiritual significance.

• This compilation includes **4,000 hymns** (Naalayira Divya Prabandham) written in Tamil, celebrating the glory of Lord Vishnu and his various forms.

• The Alvar saints were twelve prominent Vaishnavite saints who lived between the **6th and 9th centuries CE** and expressed their devotion through poetry.

• The hymns in the Divya Prabandham cover themes like **bhakti (devotion), surrender, and divine love**, making it a cornerstone of Tamil Vaishnavism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Ettutogai:** 

• Ettutogai is a collection of classical Tamil literary works belonging to the Sangam period (circa 300 BCE–300 CE).

• It consists of eight anthologies, including works like **Ahananuru, Purananuru, Kuruntokai**, and others, focusing on themes of love and war.

• It is not related to Vaishnavite devotional literature but reflects the socio-cultural aspects of ancient Tamil society.

• **Tipitaka:** 

• Tipitaka, meaning "Three Baskets," is the sacred scripture of Buddhism, written in the Pali language.

• It comprises three parts: **Vinaya Pitaka** (disciplinary rules), **Sutta Pitaka** (teachings of Buddha), and **Abhidhamma Pitaka** (philosophical analysis).

• It is entirely distinct from the Vaishnavite tradition of the Alvar saints.

• **Adi-Puran:** 

• Adi-Puran is a Jain scripture written by Jinasena, focusing on the life stories of Rishabhdev, the first Tirthankara.

• It delves into Jain philosophy and ethics, making it unrelated to the hymns of the Alvar saints.

• **Divya Prabandham:** 

• The Divya Prabandham is central to the Tamil Vaishnavite tradition and is recited in temples during rituals and festivals.

• It forms the basis for the liturgical practices in many Vaishnavite temples, including **Sri Rangam**, one of the most famous temples dedicated to Lord Vishnu.

• The hymns are still preserved and celebrated for their linguistic beauty and spiritual depth, showcasing the cultural richness of Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Compilation:** The Divya Prabandham is considered a divine revelation and was compiled by **Nathamuni**, a Vaishnavite scholar, in the 9th century CE.

• **Language:** The hymns are written in Tamil, making it accessible to common people while promoting spiritual and cultural values.

• **Themes:** The hymns emphasize concepts like **surrender (sharanagati)**, divine grace, and the glory of Vishnu's avatars.

• **Festivals:** Many verses from the Divya Prabandham are recited during Vaishnavite festivals like **Vaikuntha Ekadashi** and temple processions.
